messages:
Jane (Acme): Hey, hitting consistent failures when we invoke the OCR tool via the SDK after upgrading yesterday. Getting schema validation: "expected string (base64) but got null for 'document_bytes'". Errors started ~10:30 UTC. :frowning:

Maria S: Sorry to hear that — can you paste minimal repro and which SDK versions you're on? Also any proxy/wrapper in front of the request?

support-bot: New support ticket created: #SUP-1382 by Maria S

Jane (Acme): Repro below. We tested with Python and TS clients. Both return 400. No proxy. Upgraded SDKs as requested in release notes (sdk-py 1.6.0, sdk-ts 1.4.2).

```python
# python minimal repro
import base64, requests
b = open('sample.pdf','rb').read()
# this is what our app ends up sending after SDK helper
payload = {
  "tool": "ocr",
  "args": {"document_bytes": base64.b64encode(base64.b64encode(b)).decode()}
}
r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/tools/ocr/run', json=payload, headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ..."})
print(r.status_code, r.text)
```

Sanjay (sdk-ts): Can you also paste the raw request body you see on the wire (curl or captured body)? TS helper used to call `Buffer.toString('base64')` once; wonder if something doubled it.

Jane (Acme): Raw body snippet from our capture: `{"tool":"ocr","args":{"document_bytes":"Qlpo...=="}}` where the inner base64 decodes to another base64 string. So server is receiving base64(base64(bytes)). The schema validator then tries to decode expecting raw bytes and ends up with null.

Leo (sdk-py): Thanks — I can reproduce locally. Looks like helper `encode_bytes=True` default changed in 1.6.0 and there's an additional call site that wraps already-encoded strings. Repro steps: pip install redwood-sdk==1.6.0 then run snippet above. The SDK helper does `b64encode(b).decode()` and later marshaller does `b64encode(value.encode()).decode()` again when it sees `str` typed bytes.

Hao (sdk-go): Confirmed in Go too — when passing []byte via the union-type arg, the marshaller path for optional unions treats a raw `string` payload as already encoded and will base64-encode again in some edge flows. The net result is nested base64 which fails server-side schema validation.

Maria S: Any quick workaround we can give the customer while you prepare a patch? They are seeing increased error rates and some billing confusion because requests are invalidated mid-pipeline.

Sanjay (sdk-ts): Short-term workaround for TS: explicitly pass a Buffer and disable the SDK convenience wrapper: `redwood.callTool('ocr', {document_bytes: Buffer.from(await fs.readFile('sample.pdf'))})` — that ensures the marshaller takes the raw bytes path. For Python, downgrade to 1.5.3 or patch our wrapper: `args['document_bytes'] = base64.b64encode(b).decode()` and set `sdk_client._skip_double_encode = True` (internal flag, fragile). We'll document the workaround in the support ticket.

Leo (sdk-py): I'll push a hotfix branch that removes the double-wrap and add a unit test for union bytes+string paths. Patch PR: https://git.redwood/sdks/python/pull/472 (internal).

Bryan (eng-runtime): We should also make the server-side schema validation more tolerant for a short window — accept if decoding once yields valid bytes OR if decoding twice yields valid bytes, and return a deprecation warning in response header so clients see it. I'll open a rollout ticket and can put an autoscaled canary for 1 hour. Assigned: ENG-5203.

Hao (sdk-go): I filed go PR with fix + integration test: https://git.redwood/sdks/go/pull/289. ETA 4 hours to merge + publish patch release 0.9.7.

Maria S: Thanks everyone. Jane — immediate options: 1) downgrade SDK (py 1.5.3, ts 1.4.1, go 0.9.6) OR 2) apply explicit raw-buffer workaround. We'll keep you updated; I'm adding you to SUP-1382 thread for timeline and postmortem. :thumbsup:

Jane (Acme): Thanks — we'll downgrade for now. Please reply here when fixes are rolled. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:
